generation.explanation: tan(x) = sin(x)/cos(x), so it's undefined wherever cos(x) = 0. That happens at x = π/2 + kπ (±π/2 and ±3π/2 on this interval), and those are the vertical asymptotes, shown as red dashed lines. Near one of them, cos(x) gets close to 0 while sin(x) stays close to ±1, so the ratio becomes huge. Coming from the left the graph shoots up toward +∞, and coming from the right it drops toward −∞. Use the slider to move the dot toward an asymptote and watch tan(x) blow up. The curve repeats every π, which is why one identical branch sits between each pair of asymptotes.
